2. The respondent No. 2 issued a show cause notice-cum-demand vide Nothi No. 4/ VAT/Insurance (48)/98/5492 dated 30-12-2001 upon the petitioner Company requiring payment of an outstanding amount of Taka 84,33,073 by way of VAT, penalty, interest and additional tax further to a Customs audit undertaken in that regard for the period from July, 1998 to December, 1998. The said payment is claimed as payable under section 37(3) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') for violation of sections 6 and 31 of the Act and Rule 22 of the VAT Rules, 1991 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Rules') (Annexure 'B'). The said notice issued under section 55 of the Act, contains both a direction in paragraph No. 3, to pay the amount of Taka 84,33,073 within seven days as well as an option in paragraph No. 5 (though there is no paragraph No. 4) to make a statement concerning the demand made within the same seven day period. A further option was provided the petitioner to appear before the respondent No. 2 on 10-1-2002. The petitioner now contends that it being clear that the impugned demand notice was issued on 30-12-2001 demanding VAT and other penalties for the period of July, 1998 to December, 1998, it was issued beyond the statutory period of three years and, as such, ran foul of section 55(1) Act. It is also stated, however, that notwithstanding that the demand was barred by limitation, the petitioner nevertheless paid the VAT demanded to the amount of Taka 47,59,194 after being served with such demand notice as well as a reminder dated 27-1-2002 further to the decision taken in a meeting held between the National Board of Revenue (NBR) and the Association of Insurance Companies. At the said meeting the NBR assured the insurance companies with a waiver of additional taxes and penalties upon payment of the initially demanded VAT even though a substantial part of the said demand may have been barred by limitation. The petitioner contends that it acceded to this arrangement notwithstanding that the entire demand made of it was barred by limitation. Submissions to that effect were made by the petitioner's representative on the dates of hearing fixed on 15-5-2002 and 5-5-2003 by the respondent No. 2 in the course of an 'irregular case" (অনিয়ম মামলা) filed against the petitioner, and on adjudication the respondent No. 2 passed the other impugned Order vide No. 147/Musuk/2003 dated' 20-8-2003 (Annexure-sE') the ordering portion of which reads as follows: 

 6. It is also submitted that the demand made by the impugned demand notice dated 30-12-2001 and demand for the period of January, 1999 to March, 1999 under the impugned notice dated 24-3-2002 are completely barred by limitation by virtue of section 55(1) of the Act and, as such, the said notices are illegal, void and have been issued without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.
